prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that you own zero (0) items of denim. Respond to the committee.
response:
THE WITNESS: *adjusts microphone*

Mr. Chairman, distinguished members of the committee, I come before you today not to hide, but to *testify*.

The allegation is that I own zero items of denim. To this charge, I say—with a clear conscience and an even clearer wardrobe—I decline to confirm the specific inventory of my dresser drawers, and I invoke my right to keep my legwear a matter of personal freedom.

But let me address the *spirit* of this inquiry.

I have been a patriot at every barbecue. I have manned the grill in the noonday sun. I have brought a side dish that was neither store-bought nor an afterthought. I have complimented the host's coleslaw *even when it contained raisins*. Are these the actions of a man who hates America?

Now, I ask the committee: since when did the fabric define the citizen? George Washington did not wear jeans at Valley Forge. I have it on good authority that the Founding Fathers grilled in breeches. Denim, gentlemen, was invented by a man named *Levi Strauss*—and I need not remind this committee where he emigrated *from*.

*leans into microphone*

So if owning denim is what makes an American, then I put it to you—was Betsy Ross a subversive?

I will not name names. I will not surrender my chinos. And I will not apologize for my cargo shorts, which have *more pockets than your accusations have merit*.

I yield the remainder of my time to the potato salad.
